_meta.description: Live macro themes affecting currencies but not on the scheduled news calendar. Update as regime-changing events happen. Scanner reads this at brief generation time and displays it in the daily/weekly review.
_meta.howToUse: Each theme should include: (1) short title, (2) start date, (3) currency implications with brief reasoning, (4) a specific watchLevel that would invalidate the theme, (5) affectedPairs for scanner correlation. Retire themes by moving to _retired[] with an endDate.

themes.title: Canada-US trade war escalating — USDCAD at 1.4245 (near 52-wk high); Oct 14 US softwood lumber Section 232 binary; Jan 1 2027 50% auto/wood overhang; BoC Oct 28 binary; Canada partial de-escalation Sep 1 insufficient offset
themes.summary: As of October 1, USDCAD has surged to approximately 1.4245-1.4248, approaching its 52-week high of 1.4248, up sharply from ~1.387 in early September — a ~370-pip rally in less than a month that clearly meets the 30+ pip daily impact filter. The tariff war structural stack remains heavily loaded: US Section 338 50% tariffs on ~C$27.6 billion of Canadian goods live since Aug 22; Canada's 700+ goods-line retaliation at 15%-50% live since Sep 8; Trump's federal-contracts ban unrevoked; Jan 1 2027 structural overhang of 50% tariff escalation on kitchen cabinets and vanities (wood products). The next concrete near-term binary is October 14, when the US imposes a new 10% Section 232 tariff on softwood lumber and a 25% tariff on certain upholstered wooden products — adding to the existing ~35% AD/CVD rate stack on Canadian lumber (combined effective rate approaching ~45-47% for major producers). Additionally, the US Secretary of Commerce was due to provide Trump an update on hardwood timber and lumber imports by October 1, which may lead to further tariff proclamations. Canada partially de-escalated on September 1 by eliminating ~C$44.2 billion of counter-tariffs (the March 4 and March 13 packages, covering ~$30B and ~$14.2B in US goods), a meaningful diplomatic gesture that was insufficient to unlock a formal negotiation framework — US-origin tariff pressure on Canadian goods has continued to escalate. The Bank of Canada next meets October 28; the stagflationary dilemma persists (Canada lost ~42,000 jobs in August, unemployment at 6.4%, tariff-driven inflation pass-through ongoing). The oil variable remains a two-way binary: WTI has retreated to below $88/barrel as of October 1, Brent near $98, with US-Iran talks stalled — oil is no longer providing a meaningful CAD commodity support offset at these levels. USDCAD trading at channel resistance near 1.4245; the RoboForex H4 technical setup as of Oct 1 shows a pronounced upward wave with consolidation potential directly below resistance, suggesting tactical pause risk before the Oct 14 catalyst.

themes.title: BOJ hiked to 1.25% Sep 18 (7-2); Oct 30 BOJ next binary with Quarterly Outlook Report; Sep 30 Summary of Opinions confirms faster-hike voices; USDJPY at ~158.10 with 160.00 intervention ceiling intact; end-Oct dual binary FOMC+BOJ within 48hrs
themes.summary: As of October 1, USDJPY is trading at approximately 157.90-158.30, recovering from the September 25-26 low near 157.18 and approaching the prior week-high of 158.365 (Sep 23). The fundamental backdrop for the yen remains mixed but with incrementally hawkish BOJ signals: the BOJ's September 30 Summary of Opinions confirmed that some policymakers see a need for faster rate increases, reinforcing the October 30 BOJ meeting as a live binary. Separately, the quarterly Tankan survey published October 1 showed the strongest business confidence among Japanese major manufacturers in eight years, though the headline sentiment score for major manufacturers printed slightly below consensus estimates. The next BOJ decision is confirmed for October 30 (not October 28 as previously noted), simultaneous with the Quarterly Outlook Report — the most policy-signaling-rich meeting format on the BOJ calendar. The Sep 18 hike to 1.25% (7-2 vote) was the highest rate since April 1995 and came just three months after the prior increase — the shortest interval between BOJ hikes since 1990 — following increased pressure from Washington including calls from US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent for higher rates. BOJ board member Kazuyuki Masu has stated the central bank will continue raising its policy rate as underlying inflation nears 2%, with BOJ projecting inflation to remain above 2% in coming years and analysts forecasting price growth approaching 3% by early 2027. The US-Japan rate differential (Fed at 3.75-4.00% vs BOJ at 1.25% = 250bp) keeps carry trade structurally attractive above 157, but the October FOMC hike odds collapse (from ~70-75% to ~35-38%) has modestly compressed the expected rate gap widening, creating a slight structural USDJPY headwind at the margin. USDJPY has shown a 7-day decline of -0.41% and a monthly decline of -2.08% — consistent with an ongoing but slow structural yen appreciation trend on BOJ normalization. The critical end-October dual binary remains: Oct 27-28 FOMC (now only ~35-38% hike odds, December now ~74-76%) followed immediately or concurrently by Oct 30 BOJ (Outlook Report; policymakers signaling faster hikes). The intervention ceiling at 160.00 remains firmly intact.

implications.JPY: BOJ at 1.25% (7-2) Sep 18 — shortest interval between hikes since 1990. Oct 30 BOJ next binary with Quarterly Outlook Report: Summary of Opinions (Sep 30) confirms faster-hike voices among policymakers. Masu: will continue raising rates as inflation nears 2%. Tankan (Oct 1): strongest manufacturing confidence in 8 years but slightly below consensus. Rate gap with US (3.75-4.00% vs 1.25% = 250bp) keeps carry structurally attractive; October FOMC hike odds collapse to ~35-38% modestly reduces expected gap widening. USDJPY -2.08% monthly, -0.41% weekly — slow structural JPY appreciation trend intact. End-October critical dual event: Oct 27-28 FOMC (~35-38% hike odds, hold favored) immediately followed by Oct 30 BOJ (hawkish Outlook Report risk) — dovish FOMC hold + hawkish BOJ Outlook = USDJPY drops toward 153-155; hawkish FOMC hike + dovish BOJ = USDJPY rally toward 159-160 and intervention maximally tested.

themes.title: October FOMC hike odds collapsed to ~35-38% after softer Aug PCE and Williams 'no rush'; December hike now ~74-76% primary binary; DXY at 101.64 (highest since June); G10 rate divergence re-priced around December; NFP Oct 2 and CPI Oct 14 are the critical swing data
themes.summary: As of October 1, the post-FOMC rate divergence regime has undergone a material repricing in the last four days: October 27-28 FOMC hike probability has collapsed from ~69-75% (as of Sep 25) to approximately 35-38% (CME FedWatch / Kalshi / DeFi Rate as of Sep 30), with a hold now the modal outcome at ~66% odds and a cut at ~2%. The catalyst was a double-hit of dovish signals: (1) August PCE inflation came in below expectations — headline PCE +0.3% MoM (vs +0.4% exp) and core PCE +0.2% MoM (vs +0.3% exp), with 52% of PCE subcomponents still rising above 3% but the print itself generating immediate dovish repricing; (2) NY Fed President John Williams stated explicitly on September 29 that 'there is no reason to hurry' and that one more hike 'later this year' is appropriate but the September increase had 'bought policymakers time' — this single comment pushed October hike odds from ~70% to ~50% intraday (Seoul Economic Daily), with subsequent data confirming the collapse to 35-38%. Goldman Sachs has formally pushed its next-hike call from October to December, citing a 'strong chance' the FOMC may ultimately conclude additional hikes are unnecessary as core PCE tracks below FOMC projections. December 9 FOMC hike probability now stands at approximately 74-76% (DeFi Rate / Kalshi), making December the new primary Fed binary. The DXY, paradoxically, has rallied to 101.64 on October 1 — its highest level since June 2026 and up 2.05% over September (its strongest monthly performance since June) — reflecting broad USD resilience, carry demand, and global risk-off flows into month-end rather than October hike pricing. The 10-year UST yield has risen to approximately 5.304% (per getleveraged.com Oct 1 recap), its highest since May 2002, driven by term premium and supply concerns rather than Fed hike expectations — creating an unusual configuration where yields are rising as hike odds fall. The G10 rate divergence map remains structurally USD-bullish: Fed at 3.75-4.00% vs ECB (hold), RBA (hold), RBNZ (hold), SNB (easing), with December hike at ~74-76% maintaining the tightening cycle intact. The two pivotal near-term data releases are: (1) September NFP on October 2 — a strong print (above 200K) would immediately re-price October hike odds back toward 50%+; a weak print (below 100K) would cement the December-or-later narrative; (2) September CPI on October 14 — the most consequential inflation print before the October 27-28 FOMC.

implications.USD: DXY at 101.64 (highest since June 2026, +2.05% September). October FOMC hike odds at ~35-38%; December at ~74-76%. 10yr UST at ~5.30% (highest since May 2002) — term premium/supply driven, not hike-expectation driven. USD broadly supported by rate differential and carry despite October hike de-pricing. Recovery above 102.00 = October hike back on table; sustained break below 100.00 = December hike doubt building.
implications.EUR: EURUSD bearish — ECB on hold while Fed December hike at ~74-76%. DXY at 101.64 applies structural downward pressure. EURUSD: immediate support area near 1.1200-1.1240; bounce above 1.1400 = October hike fully dead and December doubts building. 10yr UST-Bund spread widening (10yr UST ~5.30%) provides further structural EURUSD headwind.
implications.GBP: GBPUSD under structural pressure from Fed-BoE divergence and DXY at 101.64. October NFP (Oct 2) and September CPI (Oct 14) are key GBPUSD swing inputs before Oct 27-28 FOMC. GBPUSD below 1.3200 is next target if December hike fully re-priced and DXY pushes toward 102-103.
implications.JPY: USDJPY at ~158.10 — Fed at 4.00% (potentially 4.25% in December at ~74% odds) vs BOJ at 1.25% is 250bp rate gap keeping carry structurally attractive. October FOMC hold now modal (66%) which is mildly JPY-positive at the margin; but BOJ Oct 30 Outlook Report with hawkish Summary of Opinions is the primary JPY catalyst in the near term. End-October is the critical dual event within ~48hrs.
implications.CAD: USDCAD at 1.4245 near 52-week high — tariff war fundamentals dominant, USD rate advantage (December hike ~74-76% intact), Oct 14 softwood lumber tariff binary, BoC Oct 28 binary. October FOMC hold probability (66%) may temporarily reduce one USD tailwind but structural tariff-war CAD weakness dominates.
implications.AUD: AUDUSD under pressure — RBA on hold while Fed December hike at ~74-76% primed. 10yr UST at ~5.30% compresses Australia-US rate appeal. WTI at ~$88 partially supportive but DXY at 101.64 headwind dominates. AUDUSD bias toward 0.67-0.68 area.
implications.NZD: NZDUSD bearish — RBNZ rate path less hawkish than Fed December binary. Same dynamic as AUD. NZDUSD toward 0.5750 area.
implications.CHF: USDCHF bullish — SNB in easing mode while Fed at 4.00%, December hike at ~74-76%. DXY at 101.64 applies upward USDCHF pressure. 10yr UST at ~5.30% vs SNB near-zero policy adds structural carry appeal.
